audit.why: 56.09% over 419 games matches the chart: Camille owns levels 1-5 against a Kassadin whose only pre-6 combat tool is Null Sphere (9/8.5/8/7.5/7s), and level 6 is a skill phase because The Hextech Ultimatum anchors him but Riftwalk arrives the same level. The mirror file audits/top/kassadin__camille.json reaches the same stage-by-stage split, so both directions agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two-item window was described as his because of an 'anti-AP passive shield', and the page told you to 'punish his Riftwalk cooldown'. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s - there is no cooldown to punish. Mana is his limit.
audit.why: Riot: 'Kassadin teleports to a nearby location... Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana.' Riftwalk cooldown 5/3.5/2s per champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json.
audit.corrected: winCon, dosFull[0].d, content.late and content.spikes[3].text now name the real limiter (mana and Rod of Ages timing) and stop promising a cooldown window that does not exist.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interaction errors. (1) 'his passive magic shield' / 'anti-AP passive shield' in five places - Kassadin's passive is Void Stone, flat reduced magic damage plus unit-collision immunity; the magic SHIELD comes from Null Sphere (Q). (2) 'your R's magic DoT' - The Hextech Ultimatum adds bonus magic damage to her basic attacks, it is not a damage-over-time. (3) Nether Blade (W, 7s) is an auto-attack reset and was never mentioned, so his burst tell was missing. Camille's Hookshot was also called a stun throughout; Riot's text says it knocks up.
audit.why: Riot: Void Stone - 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision.' Null Sphere - 'the excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' Nether Blade - 'Kassadin's next basic attack deals significant bonus magic damage.' Camille R - 'she also deals bonus magic damage to the target with her basic attacks.' Camille E - 'leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing.'
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text, whys[1], whys[6], early and late now name Null Sphere as the shield source and Void Stone as flat magic reduction; early adds the Nether Blade auto-reset tell; every Hookshot 'stun' becomes a knock-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: The punishable cooldown was named as Riftwalk. It is Null Sphere.
audit.why: Null Sphere is 9s at rank 1 and is his only tool to stall your gap-close; Riftwalk is 5s and cannot be waited out.
audit.corrected: content.early and wants.foe[0] now key the all-in to Null Sphere being spent.

edits.after: With Q, W and E online you run him down on cooldown — pull him into W's outer edge for max-HP damage plus a heal, then land the Q recast, whose true damage cuts straight through the Null Sphere magic shield.

edits.after: Once Kassadin stacks Riftwalk off a Rod of Ages base he blinks every trade, and Void Stone's flat magic reduction blunts the bonus magic damage your R adds — this window is his, not yours.

edits.after: He out-scales hard: stacked Riftwalk and Rod of Ages let him blink in, burst, and blink out, and Void Stone's flat magic reduction eats part of your R's bonus magic damage — so let your team body him late.

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the weakest melee laners pre-6 — his only combat tool is Null Sphere, a single silence that grants him a magic shield, and he has no Riftwalk escape until level 6. You're also thin at level 1 with just one ability, so don't waste a Q poke into his shield — deny his CS and set up your level 2 instead. From 2 onward auto into Q and wait the recast for the bonus true damage. Respect only his Q: if he silences you mid-E or mid-combo he can stall a few seconds, so bait it before you commit your gap-close.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest melee laners pre-6 — his only combat tool is Null Sphere, a silence whose leftover energy shields him against magic, and he has no Riftwalk escape until level 6. You're thin at level 1 with one ability, so deny his CS and set up your level 2 instead. From 2 onward auto into Q and wait the recast for the bonus true damage. Nether Blade (W, 7s) is an auto-attack reset — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. Bait Null Sphere, 9s at rank 1, before you commit your gap-close: silenced mid-combo you lose the Q recast.

edits.before: Kassadin is the textbook hyperscaler who reclaims the 2+ item window — with Rod of Ages, a Catalyst sustain base, and stacked Riftwalk he blinks onto your carries, bursts, and blinks out before your E or R comes back. You can't reliably pin a fully-online Kassadin, and his anti-AP passive shield soaks a big slice of Hextech Ultimatum's magic damage, blunting your one lock-down. So win the map early: splitpush to drag him to a sidelane, take towers, and close the game before his blink-and-burst pattern makes him untouchable.
edits.after: Kassadin is the textbook hyperscaler who reclaims the 2+ item window — with Rod of Ages, a Catalyst sustain base, and stacked Riftwalk he blinks onto your carries, bursts, and blinks out before your E or R comes back. Riftwalk is a 5/3.5/2s cooldown, so mana limits him, not a timer you can wait out. Void Stone's flat magic reduction also shaves the bonus magic damage your R puts on your autos, blunting your lock-down. So win the map early: splitpush to drag him to a sidelane, take towers, and close before that blink-and-burst pattern makes him untouchable.

edits.after: Spend Null Sphere's silence on your gap-close or R cast to stall you, then farm safely under tower and bank mana through your dives

notes: CHAMPION-LEVEL: Camille's Hookshot (E) is called a stun in the boilerplate across every Camille matchup in both layers. Riot's text says it knocks up on landing. I swapped it wherever it appeared in this matchup, but the same wrong wording is templated into the other 70 Camille matchups and into what-kills-me.js-style shared copy — worth a single global pass rather than 71 hand fixes. KIT FLAG MISFIRES: camille.json flags E as 'projectile' (it is a wall-anchored dash, not a missile) and R as 'channel' and 'untargetable' (Riot's text says she dashes to the target and anchors them; nothing about a channel or untargetability). I trusted the descriptions and wrote neither. _missing-interactions.json lists no Kassadin entry that contradicts this.
